newsitem.title: ITALY: Any Italy mini-budget would cut spending-Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Any Italy mini-budget would cut spending-Ciampi.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Sunday that Italy would act on spending if it decided to pass a mini-budget early this year.

Ciampi earlier told a foreign exchange conference that Italy was ready to take further steps if necessary to meet a three percent deficit-to-gross domestic product ratio needed to join a single European currency.
"The question is still open (on additional budget measures in 1997)," Ciampi told reporters after his speech.
"We are waiting for the first indications from the state accounts for the end of 1996 and start of 1997. But if an additional effort is needed it will be on the spending side."
The state accounts are due in late February or early March.
